ST154.theorem: For a finite-dimensional unital dephasing semigroup generated by Hermitian interaction observables L_k, the Heisenberg fixed algebra is the joint commutant of {H,L_k}. Consequently an environment can select an algebra without naming that algebra as output, but the interaction observables themselves are typed input. For the strict-only choice L=A the fixed algebra has dimension 22, not the desired M12 direct-sum C algebra.

ST155.boundary: Uncovered parts of the 15-dimensional fold domain may contain additional roots; multistart representatives are not a topological domain cover.

ST155.scope: This is a union of certified neighborhoods around multistart representatives, not a cover of the full 15-dimensional filtered domain.
ST155.theorem: Every accepted Krawczyk box contains exactly one fold root. If the same center has the earlier radius-1e-7 existence box and a larger accepted box, uniqueness of the larger box proves the intervening max-norm shell contains no other root.

ST156.boundary: The unitary family, prior, syndrome coupling, pinching, and readout channel are supplied. Nonorthogonal unitary errors require a different optimization.

ST156.theorem: For any finite Hilbert-Schmidt-orthogonal unitary error family {U_a} with prior p_a and classical syndrome channel q(y|a), the inverse-unitary decision U_a^dagger chosen by maximum posterior p_a q(y|a) is optimal, and F_e^*=sum_y max_a p_a q(y|a).

ST157.boundary: The Euclidean preparation metric, horizon, power interpretation, preferred outcome, and gap are supplied; this is not a strict physical action or energy theorem.
ST157.theorem: For absolutely continuous probability paths from the uniform distribution to any endpoint satisfying p0-pj>=g, the kinetic action (1/2) integral_0^T ||p_dot||_2^2 dt is at least 11g^2/(24T). The straight path to the symmetric least-asymmetric endpoint attains equality. Under pointwise kinetic power at most P_max, time is at least sqrt(11/12)g/sqrt(2P_max).

ST158.boundary: C12 geometry fixes the anisotropy shape and projection factor but does not determine the coupling g, its sign, units, or dynamical origin.
ST158.object: Minimal Local Source Shape for C12 Anisotropy
ST158.theorem: On the normalized first real Fourier mode psi_j=(r/sqrt(6))cos(theta+2pi j/12), every local even monomial sum_j psi_j^(2m) with 2m<12 is angularly isotropic. Degree twelve is the first local even monomial that aliases to cos(12theta), with the exact coefficients shown.

ST159.boundary: This disproves the ST148 single-box failure as a root-loss boundary, but it does not locate the maximal continuation domain or prove global beta optimality.
ST159.object: Adaptive Interval Cover Beyond the Single-Box Boundary
ST159.theorem: The 4x4x4 partition covers the complete declared nuisance cube. Strict local Krawczyk inclusion in every cell proves a unique stationary root inside the cell-specific root box for every nuisance triple in the global cube.

ST160.boundary: Refinement graphs, retained vertices, degree parities, and twist variables remain supplied; no strict fractal refinement law is derived.
ST160.theorem: For a rooted all-odd refinement DAG in which every vertex is reachable, path-independent F2 twists are exactly vertex coboundaries b_uv=phi_u+phi_v, so the coherent space has dimension |V|-1. A coarse-graining retaining a subset of vertices pushes a coherent twist forward by restricting phi; it is surjective, and its kernel has dimension equal to the number of eliminated nonroot vertices. For mixed parity, equality of affine linear parts on every contracted path is an additional necessary obstruction.

ST161.boundary: Tomographic completeness, instrument labels, exact matrix data, and identification with physical regions are supplied. Robust noisy reconstruction remains open.
ST161.object: Atomic Causal-Net Reconstruction from Instrument Tomography
ST161.theorem: If two labeled tomographically reconstructed instrument algebras are commuting full M2 factors, each equals the commutant of the other and together they generate M4. The tensor-factor net is then unique up to local unitaries; labels remove the remaining swap. A single abelian instrument has an eight-dimensional commutant and cannot identify the factor net.

ST162.boundary: The transition law, stationary state, and strongly separated emissions are supplied; the pair-path exponent is a conservative bound, not the exact asymptotic Chernoff rate.
ST162.object: Certified Fully Hidden Non-Erasure HMM Discrimination
ST162.theorem: For 0<s<1, subadditivity (sum a)^s <= sum a^s expands the observed HMM Chernoff coefficient into a positive four-state pair-path transfer bound. At s=1/2 every row sum is below one, proving a positive discrimination exponent even though no output symbol reveals the hidden availability state.

ST163.boundary: The bound constrains total generator norm and qudit-site locality. Microscopic qubit locality, Lieb-Robinson geometry, controls, beta, units, and apparatus remain supplied or open.
ST163.object: Finite-Time and Site-Local Bath Resource Bounds
ST163.theorem: If the total dilation generator has operator norm at most g and gt<=pi, then ||E_t-Id||_diamond<=4 sin(gt/2). Triangle inequality against the Gibbs replacement channel gives t >= (2/g)asin((2(1-gamma_min)-epsilon)/4) for epsilon-approximation. The exact isospectral two-qudit SWAP is site-local, has norm g, and completes at pi/(2g); bath dimension at least 12 remains necessary for exact reset.

ST164.boundary: The criterion is complete but the full extreme-point list beyond the partition family is not enumerated.
ST164.criterion: Write H=VV^T with row vectors v_i in R^r and let Z be the zero off-diagonal positions. H is extreme iff the only R in Sym_r satisfying v_i^T R v_i=0 for every i and v_i^T R v_j=0 for every (i,j) in Z is R=0.
ST164.object: Dimension and Complete Linear Extremality Criterion for the Minimax Spectrahedron
ST164.theorem: The optimizer set has affine dimension 66. The displayed linear criterion is necessary and sufficient for extremality. Every set partition of twelve labels yields one extreme block-correlation matrix, giving at least Bell(12)=4,213,597 distinct extreme points.

central_verdict: A typed environment can generate a fixed observable algebra, but strict A alone selects its 22-dimensional commutant rather than the desired fine-blind algebra. The C12 lattice fixes the first possible local anisotropy shape at degree twelve but not its coupling. Adaptive subdivision extends the stationary-root theorem beyond the old single-box boundary. A fully hidden HMM can retain a certified positive exponent, and thermal reset carries independent dimension and time costs. The operational completion therefore requires explicit typed resources.
epistemic_boundary: No strict environment coupling, strict fine algebra, QW-2191 discharge, strict anisotropy coefficient, dimensional unit, laboratory apparatus or record, legacy-to-strict completion or role transfer, Standard Model, gravity, L_total, physical projection theorem, or ToE closure is claimed.
